lines.japanese: 「はややっ、どうしよう吉川さん、ハンドミキサー回しすぎちゃった」
lines.english: “Uh-oh. What do I do, Yoshikawa? I ran the hand mixer too long.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……ううん、これくらいならぜんぜん平気だよ」
lines.english: “Oh... No, this much is totally fine.”

lines.japanese: 「そかー、よかったー、えへへっ」
lines.english: “Oh, good. Hee-hee.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ！　羽田さん、電話鳴ってる！」
lines.english: “Haneda! The phone's ringing!”

lines.japanese: 「わわ、ほんとだ、早く手ふいて出なきゃ……ひああっ！」
lines.english: “Wah, you're right! I need to wipe my hands and answer it... Hyaah!”

lines.japanese: 「あーっ、羽田さん大丈夫ー！？」
lines.english: “Haneda! Are you okay?!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あうう、でんわー、でんわー。どうしよう、大事な電話だったらどうしよう、早く出なきゃ、早く出な……きゃああ！」
lines.english: “O-owww. The phone! The phone! What if it's important? I have to answer. I have to answe—aaah!”

lines.japanese: 「は、羽田さぁーん！」
lines.english: “H-Hanedaaa!”

lines.japanese: 単純に電話の着信音が眠りを妨げたのか、あるいは愛しの小鳩さんが声なき祈りを送ってきたのか。
lines.english: Perhaps the ringing phone simply disturbed my sleep, or perhaps my beloved Kobato had sent me a silent prayer.

lines.japanese: どちらが発端かは分からないけれど、気付いたとき俺は飛びおきて廊下の電話に飛びついていました。
lines.english: I couldn’t say which it was, but before I knew it, I’d jumped up and rushed to the phone in the hall.

lines.japanese: 渉外担当の外交官は、楽しいお喋りからセールスのお断りまで、あらゆる局面でプリンセス・ダヴの口代わりを務めさせていただきますコンバンワ！
lines.english: As the diplomat in charge of foreign relations, I shall speak for Princess Dove in every situation, from pleasant conversation to refusing a sales pitch. Good evening!

lines.japanese: 「ハイもしもし、こちら千歳……もとい、羽田でございます！」
lines.english: “Hello, Chitose resi—no, this is the Haneda residence!”

lines.japanese: 『いいえ、あなたは成田だ』
lines.english: “No. You are Narita.”

lines.japanese: 「襲名電話！？」
lines.english: “A phone call to rename me?!”

lines.japanese: 『ドラ、大変なことが起こりました』
lines.english: “Dora, a serious thing has occurred.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、アリスさん。どうかしたの？」
lines.english: “Oh, Alice. What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 『はい、どうかした。私は買えない、商品。なぜなら、それはとても高価だった』
lines.english: “Yes, something is wrong. I cannot buy the product. Because it was very expensive.”

lines.japanese: 「あらま、それは大変」
lines.english: “Oh, dear. That's terrible.”

lines.japanese: などと驚いてみせながら、実はよく分かってないので、まず手早く現状把握のため周囲の様子を見渡してみます。
lines.english: I made a show of surprise, but in truth I had no idea what she meant, so first I took a quick look around to assess the situation.

lines.japanese: おっと、首を伸ばしてダイニングを覗きこんでみれば、小鳩さんとお友達のあきらさんがケーキ作りにいそしんでいるじゃありませんか。
lines.english: When I craned my neck into the dining room, there were Kobato and her friend Akira, hard at work making a cake.

lines.japanese: となると、いまアリスさんは材料の買い出し中……ってところかな。
lines.english: So Alice was probably out buying ingredients.

lines.japanese: 何を買いに行ったのかは知りませんが、とりあえず会話を繋ぐために──
lines.english: I did not know what she had gone to buy, but to keep the conversation going—

lines.japanese: 「──もしもし？　高いって、いくらぐらいだったの？」
lines.english: “—hello? When you say expensive, how much was it?”

lines.japanese: 『その酒は３に０がみっつも付いていた』
lines.english: “The alcohol had a three with three zeroes after it.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 微笑ましくて吹きだしそうになってしまう額でしたが、いえいえ、年齢がら彼女たちの経済力ではそれなりに大問題なのでしょう。
lines.english: I almost laughed—it was kind of sweet that this was such a crisis. But no, at their age, with their budgets, I supposed it was a pretty big deal.

lines.japanese: でもまあ、彼女らが欲しいのは、チョコケーキ作りに必要なリキュールだってことがとりあえず分かりました。
lines.english: At least I now understood that they wanted the liqueur required for their chocolate cake.

lines.japanese: ようがす、そういうことなら、このさすらいのフリーターにおまかせください。
lines.english: Very well. In that case, leave it to this wandering part-timer.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのっ、電話アリスちゃんでしたか」
lines.english: “Um, w-was that Alice on the phone?”

lines.japanese: おずおずと小鳩さんがやってきました。この反応は……ええ、気付いてるみたいですね、いま俺が千歳鷲介であることに。
lines.english: Kobato approached timidly. That reaction... Yes, she appeared to have realized that I was currently Shuusuke Chitose.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、うん。でも欲しかったやつが、高くて買えないんだって」
lines.english: “Yeah. But the thing she wanted was too expensive, so she couldn't buy it.”

lines.japanese: 「あやっ、そうなんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh, gosh. I see...”

lines.japanese: あきらさんの手前、お互い何事もないかのように会話を進めるボクらです。
lines.english: With Akira present, the two of us carried on as if nothing were out of the ordinary.

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもね小鳩さん？　実は俺、ケーキ用のリキュールだったらいいお勧め知ってるのよ」
lines.english: “But listen, Kobato. If she just needs liqueur for a cake, I know a good one to recommend.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 電話をバトンタッチしつつ、耳より情報をプレゼント。
lines.english: As I handed over the telephone, I gave her the useful tip.

lines.japanese: 「や、ちょっとね、昔バイト先で学んだんだけど、お菓子作りにはグラン・マルニエってのがいいの」
lines.english: “I learned this at an old job, but Grand Marnier is great for baking.”

lines.japanese: 「ほ、ほほー……そう、なんですか……」
lines.english: “Oh, I see... Is that so...?”

lines.japanese: 「ほらホテルなんかで出るチョコレートだと、オレンジ味のウイスキーボンボンがあるじゃない？　オレンジのリキュールを使ってるからなんだけど、そう、あれがグラン・マルニエ」
lines.english: “You know those orange-flavored whiskey bonbons they serve at hotels and places? They use orange liqueur. Right, that’s Grand Marnier.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、なるほどでしたか。でもせっかくなんですけど、私たち高いお酒は買えないのです」
lines.english: “Oh, so that's what it is. But thank you anyway. We can't afford expensive alcohol.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、でもベビーサイズがあるから、それなら５００円ちょっとで済むよ？　お菓子用なら、ちょっぴりで十分でしょ？」
lines.english: “Hmm. They sell miniature bottles too. One of those is only a little over five hundred yen. You just need a tiny bit for baking, right?”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなのがあるんですか。ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Th-they have those? Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩さんはぺこりと頭を下げると、すぐに電話口で俺に言われた通りのことを説明していました。
lines.english: Kobato dipped her head in a bow, then immediately repeated my explanation into the telephone.

lines.japanese: 「うん、そかそか」
lines.english: “Uh-huh. Okay, okay.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩さんもなんだか納得されている様子。うん、みんな幸せ。いやあ、人助けって本当にいいものですね。
lines.english: Kobato appeared convinced as well. Everybody was happy. Ah, helping people truly is a wonderful thing.

lines.japanese: 「もしもし、アリスちゃん？　あのね、いまお兄ちゃんに聞いたんだけど──」
lines.english: “Hello, Alice? Listen, I just asked Big Brother, and—”

lines.japanese: 「はー、やっぱりお兄さんすごいですー」
lines.english: “Wow. Your brother really is amazing.”

lines.japanese: 「わお！　お役に立てて光栄っす」
lines.english: “Wow! Happy to be of service!”

lines.japanese: さ、いいことしたから、また寝なおそーっと。
lines.english: Now that I'd done my good deed, it was time to go back to sleep.
